latest_session.goal: Diagnose four same-day crashes on the DTU EliteBook 840 G11 (triggered by opening Teams or a browser) and the twice-daily Windows Update prompt, a few days after a BIOS update.
latest_session.outcome: All four crashes are bugcheck `0xD1 DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL` at the same instruction offset (`...f14a`), i.e. one third-party driver. Timeline from Windows Update history: BIOS 1.10 installed via WU on 09-14 13:21; Realtek audio driver set replaced 09-15 14:46 (HD Audio 6.0.10016.1, APO 13.6437.2557.904); audio endpoints re-enumerated 09-16 09:40 and the first crash followed at 09:59, then 11:33, 13:46, 13:51. Teams and browsers initialise the audio stack on launch, so the Realtek driver is the prime suspect, BIOS secondary. The update prompt is a WU loop: "Intel - Extension - 2.1.10103.24" installed five times in a week (one failure, 0x80246007) and keeps being re-offered.
latest_session.next_steps: User to ask DTU IT to (1) roll back the Realtek audio driver and pause driver updates, (2) run `!analyze -v` on `C:\Windows\Minidump\091626-*.dmp` to confirm the driver, (3) hide or clear the stuck Intel Extension package.
